items.abstract: <jats:p>Interactions between agents are usually designed from a global viewpoint. However, the implementation of a multi-agent interaction is distributed. This difference can introduce problems. For instance, it is possible to specify protocols from a global viewpoint that cannot be implemented as a collection of individual agents. This leads naturally to the question of whether a given (global) protocol is enactable. We consider this question in a powerful setting (trace expressions), considering a range of message ordering interpretations (specifying what it means to say that an interaction step occurs before another), and a range of possible constraints on the semantics of message delivery, corresponding to different properties of the underlying communication middleware.</jats:p>
title: On Enactability of Agent Interaction Protocols: Towards a Unified Approach

items.abstract: <jats:p>Autonomous coding agents-AI systems that independently write, review, commit, and deploy software-have introduced a class of security vulnerabilities that existing application security testing methodologies cannot detect. Static Application Security Testing (SAST) and Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST), the twin pillars of modern secure development lifecycles, were designed under a foundational assumption: human developers author code, and the development pipeline consists of discrete, human-initiated events. Agentic AI systems invalidate both assumptions. This paper argues that SAST and DAST must be fundamentally reinvented, not incrementally extended, to address the threat landscape of agentic code generation. We demonstrate this gap through analysis of a representative supply chain attack vector-the adversarially poisoned AI-suggested dependency-which evades all major SAST and DAST controls by exploiting the trust model of the agent rather than the syntax or runtime behavior of the generated code. We present three contributions: (1) the Agentic Vulnerability Taxonomy (AVT), classifying vulnerability classes unique to or amplified by agentic coding pipelines across five dimensions; (2) the Agentic Risk Scoring Model (ARSM), a quantitative framework extending CVSS 3.1 with four agent-specific dimensions; and (3) the Unified Agentic Security Testing (UAST) architecture, a redesigned security testing pipeline integrating static, dynamic, behavioral, and provenance-aware analysis into a continuous, agent-aware feedback loop. These contributions are aligned with NIST AI RMF [1], ISO/IEC 42001 [2], and OWASP guidance on LLM application security [3].</jats:p>
title: Beyond SAST and DAST: A Unified Security Testing Architecture for Autonomous Coding Agents

items.abstract: <jats:p>Earth observation systems have evolved into data-rich ecosystems, yet remain limited by task-specific pipelines lacking interactive reasoning. We introduce GeoAgents, autonomous vision-language agents that synergistically combine Large Vision Models and Large Language Models to interpret, query, and reason over satellite imagery and geospatial metadata. Our system enables interactive geospatial intelligence through natural language prompts like "Where did flood extent expand between April and June 2025?" by integrating multimodal encoders, spatial grounding modules, and instruction-tuned reasoning heads. Comprehensive evaluation across multiple benchmarks demonstrates state-of-the-art performance with 92% task success rate, outperforming existing methods by 11-27% across diverse reasoning tasks. Statistical significance testing confirms our spatial grounding module improves reasoning accuracy by 12-18% compared to standard vision-language approaches (p &lt; 0.001). GeoAgents establish a new paradigm for agentic Earth observation, bridging vision, language, and decision-making for climate resilience, environmental monitoring, and humanitarian applications.</jats:p>
title: GeoAgents: Autonomous Vision-Language Agents for Interactive Geospatial Intelligence

project-title.title: Functionally Unified, Trustworthy, Ultra-Responsive, Reasoning-Enabled 6G with Autonomous Agents

project-description.description: Federated, Unified, Trustworthy, Ubiquitous Reinforcement-learning Enabled 6G through Agentic AI represents a timely and edge-cutting doctoral network addressing Europe's strategic imperative to lead autonomous 6G intelligence. At a critical moment when global competition for AI-native networking leadership intensifies, FUTURE-6G pioneers the integration of agentic AI systems—combining large language models, reinforcement learning, and multi-agent coordination—to enable zero-touch, self-managing 6G network operations aligned with the EU AI Act. This truly industrial doctorate brings together an exceptional consortium of 11 beneficiary organizations and 11 academic partners spanning world-leading telecommunications infrastructure providers (Nokia, Ericsson, Telefónica, TurkCell, Orange), cutting-edge AI hardware innovators (NVIDIA), semantic technology (ECCENCA, DTC) and RAN integration experts (IQU, ISW), and premier research institutions, creating an unparalleled innovation ecosystem where 15 doctoral candidates work embedded within industrial environments while pursuing rigorous academic training. The 15 DCs conduct research directly aligned with industry-driven challenges—from autonomous RAN orchestration and intent-driven actuation to quantum-resilient network security and energy-efficient edge intelligence—bridging the gap between academic theory and production deployment. Each doctoral researcher gains hands-on experience with production-grade network testbeds, GPU-accelerated HPC infrastructure, advanced digital twin simulation environments, and real operational networks, while contributing breakthrough innovations in agentic orchestration frameworks, hallucination-resilient LLMs, and trustworthy AI reasoning engines. FUTURE-6G delivers European technological sovereignty in AI-native network systems, creating competitive advantages through superior fault management, spectrum efficiency, energy optimization, and autonomous decisions.
